title: Should I go 3d?
author: Both_Lawfulness6708
selftext:
I wanted to make a strategy game similar to some old PC games I used to play, but for mobile. In doing so, I used different inspiration for different parts of the game.

I have the systems/mechanics done. A few bugs to work out, but other than that, I'm ready to start polishing and adding a tutorial and art.

My debate was, should I keep it 2d and simpler graphics? Or go full 3d diorama? I was planning to go 2d at first, and then do a later upgrade to 3d.

Either way, I plan on upgrading the art.

comments.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
comments.body:
This is some concept art I have for when it goes 3d.

replies.author: KurtRussel
replies.body: Honestly if you can’t make it look good in 2d you’re not gonna make it look good in 3d. Spend some time making better 2d mocks too.

replies.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
replies.body: My original plan was to create it in 2d, polish it and release it. Then later make a 3d version release separate.

replies.author: OldLead4716
replies.body: How would you plan to build the assets ? Judging by the 2d  nothing is cohesive. Planning on a using asset packs ? Generating your own ? And if you go 3d are you paying attention to target device optimization ?

replies.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
replies.body:
When I switch to 3d, I was going to use those concept images to help create a set of style images to feed into scenario. I used Grok for that image, but to keep consistent I was thinking of Flux or midjourney.

Once I have the desired style I'd have Scenario create it for the game.

If 2d, I'm not sure, I used pixel lab, but you are right that alot of that is not consistent, some images literally don't have an image for them, but it was enough that I could keep the game at the size of 1mb to keep small.

I created a flip through art bible, because, I have placement for all the art needed, just not the actual final assets.

I also have ALOT of audio I plan on adding, various background music, an advisor who speaks to explain things as well as sound effects.

replies.author: KurtRussel
replies.body:
If I can continue to make a suggestion - that’s two games and you get 1. Just make 1 game.

It does look like dogshit but so will 3d. You’re gonna have to spend a few days/weeks finding prompts and creating tools to make it look good.

The first thing I would try to figure out it blending tiles.

Like first get grass to blend. Then roads. Etc. do it in small incremental layers as opposed to some monolithic prompt.

replies.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
replies.body:
Yeah.

I ended up going for just the 3d style.

And the reasoning wasn't 2 games for one.

I literally ran into the problem of the models fighting to give me high quakity 2d art, it kept forcing 3d on me.

Also, I feel like Claude made upgrading to 3d sound like ALOT more work than it may be anyway. 🤷‍♂️

replies.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
replies.body:
Yes, so, it's literally placeholder art to keep the game lean while I worked on mechanics.

My question was upgrade 2d, or go towards the 3d concept art.

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body: It depends, you can polish now in 2D or you can 3D. If you go 3D, the time/cost in tokens required will go up drastically. Have you used software like Blender before?

replies.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
replies.body:
I have not used Blender.

I've used Pixellab and just started in Scenario.

And your right about usage, which is why I kept the file lean while making the game mechanic heavy.

Strongly inspired by games like Lord's of the Realm 2 and Romance of the three kingdoms.

I've tweaked the economy and battle components and now want to implement the art.

That's what my debate is. I plan to go 3d eventually, just wasn't sure if I should just jump to that, or polish a 2d version first.

replies.author: Both_Lawfulness6708
replies.body:
No offense taken.

Those games actually sell, and they usually are just click and watch ads.

This, while for a PC strategy game is very simple, has far more depth than those types of games.

Feed your peasants, tax them, but keep them happy enough, grow your province, manage wheat and cows/dairy for food, mine or, chop wood, quarry stone,  build armies and Castles, take over your neighbors.
